content.prompt: Write an integer that represents these scenarios:

children.label: a
children.prompt: The temperature today is 7 degrees below zero.

answer.worked: Below zero is negative, so the integer is $-7$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The carpark is 4 floors below ground.

answer.worked: Taking ground level as zero, 4 floors below ground is represented by $-4$.
The 10th floor is above ground level, so the integer is positive: $10$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Mount Everest is 8849 m above sea level.

answer.worked: Above sea level is positive, so the integer is $8849$.

children.label: e
children.prompt: The Dead Sea is 422 m below sea level.

answer.worked: Below sea level is negative, so the integer is $-422$.
A drop is a negative change, so the integer is $-3$.

inlines.text: James received $5 for doing the laundry.

answer.worked: Receiving money is a gain, so the integer is positive: $5$.
Borrowing creates a debt. Owing money is represented by a negative integer, so the integer is $-30$.

inlines.text: To work out a rule for questions where we are adding and subtracting negative numbers, like
, we will look for a pattern and come up with a rule.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}3+2&=5\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}3+1&=4\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}3+0&=3\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}(-3)+2&=-1\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}(-3)+1&=-2\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}(-3)+0&=-3\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}3-2&=1\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}3-1&=2\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}3-0&=3\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}(-3)-2&=-5\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Find the missing number.

answer.worked:
The missing addend is the difference between $23$ and $17$.
$$\begin{align*}23-17&=6\\17+6&=23\end{align*}$$

Move $17$ left to zero, then another $23$ left. The missing addend is $-(17+23)=-40$.
$$\begin{align*}17+(-40)&=17-40\\&=17-17-23\\&=-23\end{align*}$$

Move $6$ left from $-17$ to $-23$, so the missing addend is $-6$.
$$\begin{align*}-17+(-6)&=-17-6\\&=-(17+6)\\&=-23\end{align*}$$

Move $17$ right to zero, then another $23$ right. The missing addend is $17+23=40$.
$$\begin{align*}-17+40&=-17+17+23\\&=23\end{align*}$$

The starting number is $24$ less than $18$.
$$\begin{align*}18-24&=18-18-6\\&=-6\\-6+24&=-6+6+18\\&=18\end{align*}$$

The starting number is $24$ greater than $18$.
$$\begin{align*}18+24&=42\\42-24&=18\end{align*}$$

The starting number is $24$ greater than $-18$.
$$\begin{align*}-18+24&=-18+18+6\\&=6\\6-24&=6-6-18\\&=-18\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Find the missing number.

answer.worked:
The starting number is 6 units left of 8: $8-6=2$.
$$2+6=8$$

Move 6 units right to zero, then 5 more units right. Add $6+5=11$.
$$-6+11=5$$

Move 3 units right from 12 to 15, so subtract $-3$.
$$\begin{align*}12-(-3)&=12+3\\12-(-3)&=15\end{align*}$$

Move 1 unit left from $-9$ to $-10$, so add $-1$.
$$\begin{align*}-9+(-1)&=-9-1\\-9+(-1)&=-10\end{align*}$$

Move 7 units right from 13 to 20, so subtract $-7$.
$$\begin{align*}13-(-7)&=13+7\\13-(-7)&=20\end{align*}$$

Move 10 units left to zero, then 1 more unit left. Subtract $10+1=11$.
$$10-11=-1$$

Move 1 unit right from 5 to 6, so subtract $-1$.
$$\begin{align*}5-(-1)&=5+1\\5-(-1)&=6\end{align*}$$

Move 5 units right from 2 to 7, so subtract $-5$.
$$\begin{align*}2-(-5)&=2+5\\2-(-5)&=7\end{align*}$$

Move 4 units right from $-1$ to 3, so subtract $-4$.
$$\begin{align*}-1-(-4)&=-1+4\\-1-(-4)&=3\end{align*}$$

Subtracting $-3$ moves 3 units right. Start 3 units left of 7: $7-3=4$.
$$\begin{align*}4-(-3)&=4+3\\4-(-3)&=7\end{align*}$$

Subtracting $-10$ moves 10 units right. Start 10 units left of 12: $12-10=2$.
$$\begin{align*}2-(-10)&=2+10\\2-(-10)&=12\end{align*}$$

Subtracting $-4$ moves 4 units right. Start 4 units left of $-20$: $-20-4=-24$.
$$\begin{align*}-24-(-4)&=-24+4\\-24-(-4)&=-20\end{align*}$$

Move 6 units right from 5 to 11, so subtract $-6$.
$$\begin{align*}5-(-6)&=5+6\\5-(-6)&=11\end{align*}$$

Subtracting $-2$ moves 2 units right. Start 2 units left of $-3$: $-3-2=-5$.
$$\begin{align*}-5-(-2)&=-5+2\\-5-(-2)&=-3\end{align*}$$

Move 2 units left from $-2$ to $-4$, so subtract 2.
$$-2-2=-4$$

Subtracting $-5$ moves 5 units right. Start 5 units left of $-1$: $-1-5=-6$.
$$\begin{align*}-6-(-5)&=-6+5\\-6-(-5)&=-1\end{align*}$$

Move 9 units right from 6 to 15, so subtract $-9$.
$$\begin{align*}6-(-9)&=6+9\\6-(-9)&=15\end{align*}$$

Subtracting $-2$ moves 2 units right. Start 2 units left of $-4$: $-4-2=-6$.
$$\begin{align*}-6-(-2)&=-6+2\\-6-(-2)&=-4\end{align*}$$

Move 3 units left from 2 to $-1$, so add $-3$.
$$\begin{align*}2+(-3)&=2-3\\2+(-3)&=-1\end{align*}$$

Move 3 units left to zero, then 7 more units left. Add $-(3+7)=-10$.
$$\begin{align*}3+(-10)&=3-10\\3+(-10)&=-7\end{align*}$$

Move 4 units left from $-2$ to $-6$, so add $-4$.
$$\begin{align*}-2+(-4)&=-2-4\\-2+(-4)&=-6\end{align*}$$

Adding $-3$ moves 3 units left. Start 3 units right of 1: $1+3=4$.
$$\begin{align*}4+(-3)&=4-3\\4+(-3)&=1\end{align*}$$

Adding $-10$ moves 10 units left. Start 10 units right of $-11$: $-11+10=-1$.
$$\begin{align*}-1+(-10)&=-1-10\\-1+(-10)&=-11\end{align*}$$

$4$ and $-4$ form zero pairs.
$$\begin{align*}4+(-4)&=4-4\\4+(-4)&=0\end{align*}$$

Adding $-3$ moves 3 units left. Start 3 units right of 2: $2+3=5$.
$$\begin{align*}5+(-3)&=5-3\\5+(-3)&=2\end{align*}$$

Adding $-6$ moves 6 units left. Start 6 units right of $-1$: $-1+6=5$.
$$\begin{align*}5+(-6)&=5-6\\5+(-6)&=-1\end{align*}$$

Move 1 unit left from $-2$ to $-3$, so add $-1$.
$$\begin{align*}-2+(-1)&=-2-1\\-2+(-1)&=-3\end{align*}$$

$$-2\times15=-30$$
The product is negative and 5 is positive, so the missing factor is negative. Its magnitude is $30\div5=6$.
$$5\times(-6)=-30$$
The missing number is $-6$.

$$\begin{align*}-24-3&=-(24+3)\\-24-3&=-27\end{align*}$$
The product is negative and $-3$ is negative, so the missing factor is positive. Its magnitude is $27\div3=9$.
$$-3\times9=-27$$
The missing number is $9$.

$$\begin{align*}-40+4&=-36\\-2\times6&=-12\end{align*}$$
The product is negative and the known factors have a negative product, so the missing factor is positive. Its magnitude is $36\div12=3$.
$$\begin{align*}-2\times3\times6&=-6\times6\\-2\times3\times6&=-36\end{align*}$$
The missing number is $3$.

inlines.text: Jayden's bank balance is −$120 but he deposits $9 each day for the next 20 days.
On which day will his bank balance become positive?

Balances in dollars.

After 14 days:
$$\begin{align*}-120+14\times9&=-120+126\\-120+14\times9&=-120+120+6\\-120+14\times9&=6\end{align*}$$
The balance increases each day. It is negative on day 13 and positive on day 14, so it first becomes positive on the 14th day.

content.prompt: Fiona is playing a game. She throws $8$ balls at a target, one at a time. Each hit is worth $5$ points. Each miss is worth $-3$ points. Fiona hits the target with $5$ of the balls and misses with the rest.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many points does Fiona score?

answer.worked:
Number of misses: $8-5=3$.

$$\begin{align*}5\times5+3\times(-3)&=25+(-9)\\5\times5+3\times(-3)&=25-9\\5\times5+3\times(-3)&=16\end{align*}$$

Fiona scores $16$ points.

inlines.text: balls at the target, one at a time.
Is it possible for Chris to score the same number of points as Fiona?

answer.short: No. With $5$ hits and $4$ misses Chris scores $13$ points; with $6$ hits and $3$ misses he scores $21$ points. Each extra hit increases the score by $8$ points, so $16$ is impossible.
answer.worked:
With $5$ hits and $4$ misses:

$$\begin{align*}5\times5+4\times(-3)&=25-12\\5\times5+4\times(-3)&=13\end{align*}$$

With $6$ hits and $3$ misses:

$$\begin{align*}6\times5+3\times(-3)&=30-9\\6\times5+3\times(-3)&=21\end{align*}$$

Replacing a miss with a hit increases the score by $5-(-3)=8$ points. Fewer than $5$ hits give a score below $13$; more than $6$ hits give a score above $21$. Since $13<16<21$, Chris cannot score $16$ points.

presentation.content:
Syllabus Content

MA4-INT-C-01 compares, orders and calculates with integers to solve problems

Compare and order integers

  • Recognise and describe the direction and magnitude of integers
  • Identify and represent integers on a number line
  • Compare the relative value of integers using the less than (<) and greater than (>) symbols
  • Order integers

Add and subtract positive and negative integers

  • Add and subtract integers with and without the use of digital tools
  • Construct a directed number sentence to model a situation
  • Examine different meanings (position or operation) for the + and - signs, depending on context

Multiply and divide positive and negative integers

  • Represent multiples of negative integers as repeated addition
  • Multiply and divide positive and negative integers with and without the use of digital tools

Apply the 4 operations to integers

  • Apply the 4 operations to integers
  • Solve problems involving grouping symbols with integers
  • Apply the order of operations to evaluate expressions involving integers, with and without the use of digital tools

entries.description:
Integers on a Number Line
We can represent integers as values on a number line.
A negative integer is to the left of zero, or below zero.
A positive integer is the to the right of zero, or above zero.
On a number line, each interval, or gap, represents the same amount.
